title: Встреча с Родионом Сергеевичем на выкупе  (Meeting Rodion Sergeyevich at the Drop)

segments.t: Back at the kitchen, Max argues with Fedya about the contraband snails, while across town Kostya waits with Nastya's father at the ransom drop point. When homeless gentleman Rodion Sergeyevich walks up to collect the cash, Kostya cheerfully greets him by name.
А что ты меня вообще слушаешь?
А вы случайно пиво не пьете?
Родион Сергеевич, какое пиво зимой на улице?
Now let's break down each line of their conversation.
'Forgive me.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'excuse me' before landing on 'me'. Fedya answers right away.
'They are perfectly fine.' The grammar packs 'normal' and 'they' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'I just made an assumption.' Rodion brings out the contrast between 'I' and 'suppose' in a few short words.
А что ты меня вообще слушаешь?
'Why are you even listening to me in the first place?' Notice how Russian expresses 'and' and 'are listening to' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Fedya answers right away.
'And what if he does not show up?' Fedya raises the pitch on 'will come' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question.
'He will show up, where else would he go?' The grammar packs 'will come' and 'will go' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'He needs the cash, which means he will show up.' Max anchors the line on 'grand', while 'will come' completes the thought. Fedya answers right away.
'Konstantin, hello there.' In Russian, the idea of 'Konstantin' flows naturally into 'hello' without extra filler words.
А вы случайно пиво не пьете?
'Do you happen to drink beer, by any chance?' In Russian, the idea of 'and' flows naturally into 'drink' without extra filler words.
'Hello, Rodion Sergeyevich.' The grammar packs 'hello' and 'Sergeyevich' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Fedya answers right away.
Родион Сергеевич, какое пиво зимой на улице?
'Rodion Sergeyevich, who drinks beer outside in the winter?' The grammar packs 'Rodion' and 'street' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Well, one can see.' Rodion brings out the contrast between 'but' and 'one can see' in a few short words.
'Tell me who your friend is.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'say' and finishing on 'friend'. Now let's put it all back together and hear the whole scene again.
А что ты меня вообще слушаешь?
А вы случайно пиво не пьете?
Родион Сергеевич, какое пиво зимой на улице?
